name: Race data
summary: Race data for the pit wall: sector and lap times, last-5-lap averages (any last n: CarTelemetry.avg_last), the pace table (pace_ranks: last lap, last 3, last 5 per class), each car's rival (rival_of) and backmarkers (is_backmarker, backmarkers_ahead), gaps and intervals, tyre state, pit-window analysis (pit lane loss per track), weather radar and forecast (a rain field moving on a seeded wind that matches the race weather at the track, with ETA ranges from a forecaster whose speed estimate is a little off; WeatherForecast.rain_at, sample_grid, truth_at, rain_in), and a feed of strategy, radio and timing calls. Runs on every machine; the host's gaps and pit analysis are synced to clients. Every race keeps a full lap-by-lap log (to_dict) with the tyre on the car and the stops each lap, each car's grid position and every pit stop (CarTelemetry.grid_pos, stops). Damage advice for the strategist (DamageAdvice.assess): how bad a car's damage is, the lap time it costs (measured per part with tests/damage_pace_probe.gd), the repair time a stop would take (PitRules.repair_parts / service_for), what it costs to the flag, the places a repair stop gives away, and a call: box now, fix at your stop, stop but don't repair, stay out or your call.
notes: Pure data like the sim: no nodes, no clock, no Input. It only reads the RaceSim, so it never changes the race. AI teams post radio/strategy calls with RaceSim.post_event(); the feed shows them. The strategist screen (ui) draws all of this.
